clue.text: A source of cold comfort South African boy put before bank

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a bar is a bank of sand or shingle across a river mouth

explanation.surface: A South African lad stands in front of a riverbank, oddly said to bring cold comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put before' simply tells you the boy and bank come in that order after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad counter serves chilled food, a cheering but literally cold treat.

clue.text: Join a navy I did

parts.note: a seam is a join between two pieces of fabric

explanation.surface: A sailor proudly recalls enlisting for service at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the sailor himself speaks, saying he joined a navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is one who has joined a navy and can say so of himself.

clue.text: Dodges hols spent in and around windy Poole

indicators.note: the holiday letters are used up and reworked, so they are shuffled
a windy town is blown about, signalling that the letters of the place name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in blustery Poole look for ways round the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in and around' is only a link; both indicators point to one combined rearrangement. Poole is a seaside town in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopholes are ways of evading a rule, so they are dodges in the sense of tricks.

clue.text: A time to give sparklers to mates

definitions.text: A time to give sparklers to mates

parts.words: A time to give sparklers to mates
parts.note: sparklers looks like fireworks and mates like friends, but they are diamonds and spouses at a sixtieth marriage anniversary

explanation.definitionFit: The sixtieth wedding anniversaries are traditionally marked with gifts of diamonds between husband and wife.

clue.text: Collection a Roman Catholic found on a busy place

parts.note: a hive of activity is a busy place

explanation.surface: A Catholic group is discovered gathering at a bustling spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' is just a link placing the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of records or documents.

clue.text: Sycophant's first stroke — untidy writing

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word Sycophant

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A flatterer's opening move turns out to be messy handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests a pen mark, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is hurried, careless handwriting.

clue.text: Peeved with louder mobile ringing (soft zeds needed) doing this

parts.note: peeved means cross

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P stands for piano, soft in music
two zeds give ZZ

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by a loud ringing phone, while dozing, is solving the very puzzle in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' and 'needed' are only links: the phone-and-sleep picture hides that soft is the music abbreviation and zeds are letters, not snores.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue refers to the solver's current activity, tackling a cryptic grid.

clue.text: Up to date except about French battle

indicators.note: except means leaving out the following French word from the phrase

parts.note: a la mode means fashionable, up to date
de is French for of or about

explanation.surface: Something modern, minus a French connection, becomes a famous fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DE from ALAMODE leaves ALAMO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was the 1836 siege in Texas, a celebrated battle.

clue.text: Students left with the workforce

parts.note: earners are the people who make up the workforce

explanation.surface: Pupils leave and join the working population.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners are people being taught, so they are students.

clue.text: Several literary cormorants, say

definitions.meaning: an old literary word meaning several or sundry
cormorants are birds that plunge underwater for fish, an example of underwater swimmers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sundry in old writing and also names birds that plunge underwater for food.

clue.text: Whiff of espresso, say, to italy's capital

definitions.meaning: the smell of coffee is a pleasant scent
in Italian, a Roma means to Rome

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a pleasant smell, and split up it is Italian for going to Rome.

clue.text: Natter about one US politician having a little snag?

indicators.note: about means the chat letters go round the next pieces

parts.note: to natter is to chat
I is the Roman numeral one
POL is American slang for a politician

explanation.surface: Gossip about an American politician hitting a minor problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snag' looks like a small hitch, but it is Australian slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sausage is a little snag, in the Australian slang sense.

clue.text: Hop it dear" snarled goddess

indicators.note: snarled means tangled, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry divinity growls at someone to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled' looks like the way it was said, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek deity of love.

clue.text: Presently getting to grips with prison's first stirrer

indicators.note: gripping something holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: presently means soon

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of prison

explanation.surface: Soon a troublemaker grabs hold of the jail's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirrer' suggests a troublemaker, but it is a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon is used to stir food or drink.

clue.text: Distract batsman starting to slice left side

indicators.note: starting to means take only the opening letter of slice

parts.note: an edge is a side

explanation.surface: A cricketer slices the ball to the left and is put off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to sledge is to taunt the batsman to break his concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledging is verbal goading aimed at unsettling a batsman at the crease.

clue.text: Bung hat on to stand at first

indicators.note: on to means the hat is placed after that letter
at first means take only the opening letter of stand

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone told to put a hat on to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a plug or cork, something that seals a bottle.

clue.text: Column about dropped letters

parts.note: read as a newspaper column on post, it is really a pillar that encloses the mail posted into it

explanation.definitionFit: A British red post box is a pillar-shaped receptacle that holds posted mail.

clue.text: One to buy and sell is beginning to tempt dreamer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to deal is to trade

indicators.note: beginning to means take only the opening letter of tempt

explanation.surface: A trader is starting to tempt someone with lofty ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues perfect aims, a visionary or romantic.

clue.text: Escape into hollow drop

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dent is a hollow
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Fleeing into a pit means a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or fall.

clue.text: Plan diplomacy — nice at heart

parts.note: tact means diplomacy

indicators.note: at heart means take the central letters of nice

explanation.surface: A tactful scheme that is kind deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a scheme or method for achieving something.

clue.text: Pepper hot plate when last of cooking's done

indicators.note: done, as in done away with, means remove the letter

parts.note: a griddle is a hot cooking plate

indicators.note: last of means take only the final letter of cooking

explanation.surface: Season a hob once the cooking is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pepper' looks like seasoning, but it means to spray with shot; G is removed from GRIDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle with bullets is to pepper with holes.

clue.text: Reprise role I've stamped out

indicators.note: a reprise is a repeat performance done differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor repeats a part he has stopped playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamped out' looks like put out, but defines raised relief work punched from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is relief sculpture, with forms raised or hammered outward from a surface.

clue.text: Democrat with need

parts.note: and means with

explanation.surface: A US Democrat comes with a requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: A demand is a requirement or need.

clue.text: Tart caught in flat

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: flat dull country can be arid
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pastry trapped in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' and 'flat' look like a pastry and an apartment; they mean sour and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp or bitter in taste, so tart.

clue.text: Anger sermon-maker in the pulpit?

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a preacher
a preacher in the pulpit is up above the congregation

explanation.surface: A preacher losing his temper while delivering his address.
explanation.definitionFit: To rev someone up is to stir or work them up.

clue.text: Determine a cute call having been dealt

indicators.note: cards that have been dealt are shuffled first, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player decides on a clever bid after the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To calculate is to work out or determine.

clue.text: Coming up with a good idea. One I have after new release

definitions.text: Coming up with a good idea

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the earlier ones

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to vent is to release
I've is a contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone with a bright idea feels relief at having a fresh outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventive describes being creative and producing fresh ideas.

clue.text: Enthusiasm is not quite complete about brown horse

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the next piece
not quite complete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: zeal means enthusiasm
BR is the abbreviation for brown

explanation.surface: Keenness for a brown horse is lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite complete' makes ZEA, which goes round BR. The definition is loose: a zebra is a striped relative of the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra is a wild African animal of the horse family.

clue.text: One found in pool working by touch formerly?

definitions.text: One found in pool working by touch formerly?

parts.words: One found in pool working by touch formerly?
parts.note: the pool suggests swimming, but it is an office typing pool where staff worked by touch on keys

explanation.definitionFit: Typists worked in typing pools and often learned touch-typing, a job now largely gone.

clue.text: Shocked European sacked

parts.note: a Pole is a European
axed means sacked

explanation.surface: A European worker is fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Poleaxed means stunned as if struck with an axe, hence shocked.
